noticias.titulo: How Sonos rebooted itself
noticias.resumen: Today, I’m talking with Tom Conrad, the CEO of Sonos. Tom and I have known each other for a long time — he was the chief technology officer of Pandora, VP of product at Snap, and the chief product officer of Quibi. He was also on the board at Sonos during its disastrous 2024 app […]
noticias.contenido: Today, I’m talking with Tom Conrad, the CEO of Sonos. Tom and I have known each other for a long time — he was the chief technology officer of Pandora, VP of product at Snap, and the chief product officer of Quibi. He was also on the board at Sonos during its disastrous 2024 app redesign that threatened to crash the entire brand. Tom took over as interim CEO to right the ship during that period, and then took the permanent role just about a year ago. As you’ll hear him say, he thinks Sonos is fully out of that period now, and on to its next chapter with a huge product and platform launch called Sonos 27 . Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . I mean, come on, you all listen to the show. That is all the most Decoder bait imaginable. I have been dying to have Tom on the show to talk about how the board decided to move on from previous CEO Patrick Spence, how he diagnosed the issues inside the company, and what decisions he made to fix them. Those fixes involved a lot of big changes: to the company’s structure, its product lineup, and how it thinks about itself and what its product fundamentally is. That’s that new platform, Sonos 27, which you’ll hear Tom call a new foundation for the company that makes every Sonos product work better as part of a system. There’s a lot here, including how AI assistants can work across the system, the idea of having a mesh network of little computers in your home disguised as speakers, and of course, the testy relationship between Sonos and Google, which means Google’s Gemini assistant isn’t available on Sonos devices. Oh, and of course we got into the weeds about smart home standards, because I am a smart home nerd and simply cannot help myself. But to his credit, Tom was willing to nerd out with me, and I think this conversation is pretty fun because of it. Okay: Sonos CEO Tom Conrad. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Tom Conrad, you’re the CEO of Sonos. Welcome to Decoder . Thank you. As they say, it’s so great to be here. I am just going to say, finally, I have been asking you to be on the show for at least a year, if not before. I think the first time I met you was in the back of a car at CES when you were at Pandora. Sounds right. One hundred years ago. One hundred years ago. We were children. [Laughs] We were little babies. That car was driven by a human driver. That’s how far back it was. That’s right. And then you took a turn through Quibi. You and I talked through that, and now you’re at Sonos. As you know, I’m a huge fan of Sonos. We had your predecessor, Patrick Spence, on the show a bunch of times . Many things have happened, so I just want to start at the very beginning of this. You’re about a year into being the permanent CEO of Sonos. You have a bunch of news to announce. Just tell us what you think Sonos is today. What is your conception of this company? When I came in the door, one of my earliest observations was that the company behaved like it was 100 percent hardware, but we’re really 100 percent hardware and 100 percent software. And if you get either one of those even a little bit wrong, the impact is tremendous. So how does that show up really day-to-day? It was about returning the company to the idea that Sonos doesn’t make these individual products, but we really make one thing — we make the Sonos system. It all has to hang together in a cohesive, interesting, and valuable way, or we’re just not doing the work. There’s been a bunch of basic blocking and tackling, of course, both operationally and in the work that we’re doing in the product family. But at the highest level, returning the company to the idea that we are a system for audio in the home has been the highest-level mantra. When you say come into the company, do you mean as a board member or as the CEO? I mean, let’s start the starter pistol in January of 2025, 18 months ago, when I stepped in first as interim CEO and then was lucky enough six months later to be asked to take the job more permanently. The reason I asked that question is that you obviously have two different views of the company in different roles. We did have former CEO Patrick Spence on several occasions, and he said something very similar to me when he first took over — that Sonos was stuck in its ways. It was really focused on very, very slow iterations of hardware. He tried very hard to push the metabolism of the company to be much faster, and he talked about that very openly with me. That led eventually to what I think is a moment of true crisis: the app launch. It was a disaster. The system stopped working. That’s when you came in to right the ship. Tell me about that gap. You came in, and you said this company thinks it’s a hardware company. That’s what your predecessor had been saying, but it went sideways in big, meaningful ways. Tell me about that moment and why you think it was the same conception even when you came in. So as you describe, I’ve been involved with the company going back almost 20 years. We brought Pandora to Sonos in 2007, I think, and I was able to get to know the company as a partner before I got to know it as a board member. I came onto the board in 2016 right as Patrick became CEO. So from the vantage point of a board member, I got to participate in Patrick’s chapter. I guess the way I would characterize his high-order thinking about the company in those early days was that, as you described, he wanted to turn the company into a product execution machine with an emphasis on hardware products. We call them NPIs, or new product introductions. In the chapter before him, it was sometimes years between new Sonos products. Spence said, “Look, we’re going to make a company that knows how to ship a couple of great new products a year.” And he did that. I mean, the company has reliably shipped a couple of great products, hardware products, every year, for close to a decade now. Sometimes, when you energize an organization around an idea, there are unintended consequences. I think one unintended consequence of that framing was that the company became very focused on the individual products, one at a time. Even as a board member, I received Roam as a portable speaker with a certain amount of battery life, waterproofing, and Bluetooth connectivity. I didn’t really think about it as a member of the Sonos system. Even with the software work that we did, and with every product that we make, there is a tremendous amount of software effort and innovation that goes into them. But even the software that we made was very focused on the individual NPIs. “What can we do in software to differentiate Move 2 from other speakers in that category?” What was hard to do, and what was hard to prioritize in the company, was horizontal slices of software experiences that benefited all of the platform. So, in a way, I think some of that debt accumulated, and the company thought that the antidote was to recreate the app experience. And as you know, we made a bunch of mistakes at that moment. I’m really proud of the fact that I think we’re well beyond that chapter now, but we could have been much more thoughtful about how we qualified that product in the real world. We could have been much more thoughtful about how we rolled it out to customers. We could have, candidly, I think, examined the original impetus in the first place. It was very Sonos-motivated. We wanted to put the app on a modern architecture to make us more nimble. In my chapter at Sonos, I’m really trying to bring it all back to how we can focus on the customer first. I’m so inspired by talking to people on social media and in my inbox, and people in the industry, like you, about how we show up and solve the real problems that are happening in real households. I’m so excited about the things we’re going to talk to you about today because I think they’re really an answer to many of those questions. If you’re a listener, you know I’m familiar with Tom. The man’s on Threads doing customer support every day. And actually, I should not take advantage of this. I hold myself back from asking you for direct customer support all the time. Anytime. The way that you can tell it’s actually me and not our crackerjack social team is that I often will let a Thread die before I should or fail to follow up with someone. So if we were executing perfectly on that, you would know it was fake Tom, but it’s real Tom, and I do it when I can, but sometimes imperfectly. At least it’s not an AI avatar Tom. That’s when we know it’s going to go sideways. [Laughs] That’s right. I know you’re a Decoder fan, so I’m going to make you sit in this for just one more moment because I find all of this to be really fascinating. The app shipped, and the feedback was immediately and intensely negative. Many, many things were broken. Speakers weren’t working at weddings. This is a time of massive crisis. The company goes to resolve it, but then you’re on the board, and it’s clear that there’s going to be a leadership transition, that Patrick needs to go, and we need a new CEO. You’re going to be the interim CEO. Tell us about that process. Very, very few people will ever be in that kind of process or get insight into that process. What happened? What were the steps? Well, I guess you start by saying that the last thing as a board that you want to do is to remove a CEO, particularly one who had as many successes as Patrick had. But I think as we looked at the company’s progress recovering from the app crisis, and frankly the tenor of the conversation inside the company, we just decided that for this kind of step-function improvement we needed on some of these dimensions, we had to make some changes in leadership, and that included a CEO change. It was a wild experience for me because, I’ll tell you, at no point in the decade leading up to that day in January did I imagine that I might end up the CEO of Sonos. But in the process, the board asked if I’d be willing to step in on an interim basis, and it was an easy yes for me. It’s a cliché, but I’m a customer, and I love this product. There was a Sonos Move in the room when my daughter was born. You talked about weddings. I was watching friends and colleagues on the internet, frustrated by their experience. I wanted to come in and fix it. Of course, as a board member, I felt some real culpability in it. So [I was] thrilled at the chance to come in. When you’re an interim CEO, the assignment is really to keep the wheels on. The assignment at Sonos specifically was to right the ship. So during the period when the board was doing their comprehensive search for the person that they would ultimately decide was the right choice for the company, it was really easy for me to show up and just do that hard work of trying to get the company back on track. While I never imagined that I would land in this seat, I feel so blessed that it happened. I do love this job and continue to love the company and the team, and I’m so excited about the things we’re doing for our customers. Very few people are going to get an interview to become the CEO of Sonos. I imagine at some point you went from being the interim CEO to wanting to become the permanent CEO. What was that process like? Did you write a memo? Was there a pitch deck? What were the steps? Yeah, so there were a couple of pitch moments that the board asked me, completely reasonably, to engage in the process of applying for the job in the same way that all of the other talented candidates that they spoke to engaged. And so I took a personality test. Wait, you did? Yeah. With the letters? Oh, yeah. Like an ENTJ or whatever? Oh, yeah. One of the letter things, sure. They wanted to know what they were getting. Do they know that that is basically just like astrology? Someone should tell them. You know what? Yep, yep. I presented my vision for the company more than once, and I had the incredible advantage of being inside the four walls of the company and deeply understanding what was working and what wasn’t, and the things that we needed to do to get to this next chapter. It was a period of intense, intense work for me and everybody around me at the company, and more than a little anxiety about how it was going to turn out. It was so fun, though, to get the call and then to just immediately be able to pivot at least a fraction of the work from the entirely tactical to the much more strategic, to begin to talk about what kind of company we are going to build together in this next chapter. I think that in the immediate term, we’re really excited about what we can do in the use cases that our customers are telling us they care about. Give me mood and audio in the home. We have great solutions for that today. And I think we can take advantage of this shift to a truly next-generation architecture without the baggage of a decade of internet-connected light switches from 17 different protocols with 17 different hubs in the closet. Well, I mean, part of the opportunity there is that you don’t have a big voice assistant. I don’t think the current Sonos voice assistant is at the scale of Alexa or Google Assistant. I’m just guessing. They do have that problem. The light switches in my house, they’re in the walls. They’re going to be there. That Lutron hub is there. It’s not great. However, Lutron is the best one. It is. It is the best one. There’s a box in my house, and there are a lot of those little weird little boxes in my house because I have a smart home, and all of those dependencies exist for those platforms for reasons. If you show up and say, “Use my voice assistant instead,” and it can’t operate all of the lights, well, I’m just going to fall back to Amazon, or I’m going to fall back to Google. They know it, and they know they can’t break those things. Panos and I have talked about it a lot, actually in the context of Alexa Plus. The promise of AI, at least from my very abstract vantage point, is, boy, I should not care about any of this. There’s a network in my house. There are lots of devices on that network. They have some access points on that network, and maybe they’re API-driven access points, maybe they’re MCP-driven. It should not matter. There’s just a bunch of devices in my network that you can control somehow, and this all-seeing robot that is going to replace every job in America should be able to traverse my network and turn on the lights without any help. That’s what it should do. Some of the very first big vibe coding shockwaves were AI researchers, bleeding-edge AI researchers, being like, “I figured out how to control my shades. They walked through my network, and the shades go up and down now,” right? We’re not there at the consumer level. The promise is not there. I’m still here talking to you about Matter, Thread, HomeKit, and whether or not Google Assistant can control my Sonos Amp, which, by the way, it can’t, and that is my one ticket to you that I didn’t submit on Threads. That’s the promise, but the gap to that seems really, really huge. Are you able to close it? Is that the opportunity? I think we’re just still in the Apple II days of the home automation space. So while there is, as you point out, this incredible, wild, heterogeneous world of different light switch controllers, I think when you talk to mainstream consumers about their homes, they’re not there yet. I do think that because of the profound technological step function of agentic control of these kinds of services and things like tool use, as the consumer catches up with the industry’s ambition to solve these problems, new technological solutions will emerge. I’m really excited about how we’re positioned to ride that transition and not be encumbered by the decade of early adopter internet-connected light switches. What are you going to do about the light switches that are already in the walls? I just don’t think that there’s enough of them to matter in the final answer. Of course, Lutron’s a great partner, and they do a great job with this. They do. I mean, we have them. We’ve got all kinds of light switches. We mostly have Lutron ones. But that’s my question. The first natural customer for something like what you’re describing is somebody who is already using these products in some way. If you show up to my house and there’s no Matter support or whatever, I’m like, “Well, I can’t use it.” Is it though, or is it more like the difference between the people that were adopting Creative Labs MP3 players before the iPod came along? Sure . Was the iPod really for those people, or was it for people that had that problem but were nowhere near the people that had been early adopters? Or was the iPhone for people that were using Windows CE, or was it for people that were using flip phones who were ready for the transition? I think we’re making- Is that the idea here “iPhone for smart home control” or “iPhone for audio in the home”? That’s right. The turn there that I think is really interesting is: who are you going to talk to? Where is the computer? What is the computer? You’re describing a situation where if you want music, you’re going to talk to Sonos. But you also have a general-purpose assistant like Claude or ChatGPT, and they can talk to Sonos, too. It’s unclear to me — and it may be one of the most fascinating questions at this moment in tech — where the interface goes. Are we all going to have one chatbot that does everything, and all the demand is aggregated there, and OpenAI becomes more powerful than ever? Or are we going to have lots and lots of assistants that we address in lots and lots of different ways? It seems like your bet is Sonos will have a personality in your home, maybe multiple personalities in your home, and customers will address that, and all the other stuff will go somewhere else. For 20 years, we’ve found a lot of success around the idea of embracing every dimension of the problem. Yes, there’s an app, but you’re welcome to engage with us through AirPlay or Spotify Connect. Yes, we have a voice assistant that lives side by side with Alexa. Yes, we have proprietary mesh, but it integrates with Bluetooth and even line-in. I think we bet that we’re of a size and scale that allows us to both be nimble and react to these changes, but also have enough horsepower to keep up technologically with what the best in the category are doing. So I think some of this just plays out on the field. Just one last idea, since you said it a couple of times, this question about where the compute lives. I think one incredibly powerful opportunity for Sonos is that we do place compute in millions and millions of homes. People don’t think of them as computers often, but they are. They create a seamless experience that is really the integration of a set of cloud services and local services in a way that looks like just one surface area to the customer. I think that the answer to your questions, “Does this live in the cloud? Does this live in the home? Does this live in a box?” is yes. I think we’re pretty uniquely situated to take advantage of an architecture where it’s not cloud-only, it’s not home-only, but it’s an integrated system that combines all of that together. And at the end of the day, that is what Sonos 27 is. Just to make that really reductive, when I say “where is the computer” in the home context, what I mean is maybe in the ’90s to early 2000s, there was a vision that we would all have home servers in our basements, and they would do all the logic of our home. They would have all the storage, and Microsoft would sell you a Windows home server in the basement and a Windows Media Center in the living room, and you and I probably both watched all of those Bill Gates keynotes at CES. None of that really ever came to pass. Instead, we put a lot of cheap computers near all the TVs, and they connected to cloud services, and they’re basically just running web browsers, as you well know. That is a very different version of what needed to happen and how the market played out. In the smart home, I’ve got a bunch of automations in my house. When the garage is open, the lights turn on, and other stuff happens. At night, the doors all lock if they’re not locked. That logic has to live somewhere. My perspective on it is that it should live in my house. If the internet goes down, the lights should still turn on. This is not anything to do with big AI integrations or the new MCP way to address the Sonos system. Those are big ideas, and I’m just insistently dragging you back down into the dirt of: if the internet goes out, are the lights still going to turn on? You don’t want to be the partner that puts in the internet-connected light switches that don’t work when the internet is down. But it’s not just the internet-connected light switches; it’s the logic of making it all work together. I understand. Yeah, fair. Here’s what I’ll say about that. For 40 years now, we’ve been talking about technology for the home, starting with the personal computer, which is supposed to be the center of the technological household, but we didn’t really get that. We got laptops that people mostly use at work and use a bit at home. Then we got mobile, and mobile is supposed to be the thing that you engage with when you leave your house on your way to work. Of course, the fundamental media of mobile is so addicting that it’s all-consuming. We use it at work, we use it at home — we use it all the time. But my observation about our use of it in the home is that nobody loves it. No spouse has ever said, “I wish my husband was on his phone more. I wish my kid used their iPad more,” and so we’re looking for ways to get beyond that. To your point, the other compute that’s in the home, like I said, is the set-top box, which is largely just a web browser to a bunch of services that live in the cloud. I think it’s pretty interesting, actually, that in 17 million homes Sonos is an actual mesh of compute in your house with real horsepower, real memory, real CPU, real capability, a real operating system — all just waiting to be the container for some of the kinds of things you’re talking about. So it’s super interesting. We’ll figure it out over time. I feel like you’re this close to being like, “And then the Teslas will be a data center.” There’s something there that is maybe the line. Actually, I want to talk about that. I actually want to push on that a little bit. The initial Sonos innovation 100 years ago, when the company started, was, “Oh, we can build a mesh network. We can do wireless audio at scale. We can synchronize the latency of all the speakers so it sounds like the same music playing at the same time.” This was a lot of big engineering back in the day. Still, I mean, candidly, still. A lot of what our software team does day in and day out is extend and maintain that infrastructure. There are features you’re announcing here as part of Sonos Fabric that I think are interesting. If you have surrounds, you can just place them, and they’ll figure out that they’re surrounds and immediately start being the surround speakers in a home theater. There’s just a lot of potential, as you’re describing, in the notion that, “Oh, there’s a big network of small computers in my house that can come together and do things you would not expect.” Is your focus that they will always do audio things? Or is it the focus that they will have many more capabilities? I think any thoughtful product leader is going to tell you the focus is an important part of success. I do feel like there’s so much interesting work for us to do around creating an audio system that sets the mood for your home that I don’t want us to take our eye off of that opportunity. We are doing some really exciting things in Sonos Fabric and Sonos 27 that we should talk about, that get to some of the work that you’re describing. But certainly in the moments where you allow yourself to think about what the company is in five years and what it will be in 10 years, you can’t help but interrogate what the opportunity is for a mesh — a fabric of compute that lives in the home. I want to end by talking about headphones really quickly. We just had the CEO of Bose on. She and I had a pretty searching conversation about what happens to the headphone market in the time of AI wearables. My fear, my anxiety, about audio is always that consumers will always pick convenience over quality. It’s just the history of the… I’ve got a set of AirPods on this desk, and they don’t sound great, but boy, are they convenient. And that’s just the way it goes. It has always been what the market has demanded: convenience over quality. We’re going to enter a time when Apple puts cameras on AirPods, and you can talk to them with Siri. When Google and Samsung ship very similar products, there’s undoubtedly going to be a flood of AI hardware startups that want to put something in your ears or in your body in some way. You are in the headphone market. You’re talking a lot about AI; you’re talking a lot about Fabric. That seems like a cataclysm coming for headphones. The same way that the removal of the headphone jack was a cataclysm in the headphone market, this seems like the next one. How are you preparing for that? Do you think there’s going to be a range of voice assistants on headphones, or do you think what you would call the first-party vendors are going to just grab more and more of that share? Before we jump to the hypotheticals about where headphones are, can I tell you a little bit about the new headphones? Yeah, of course. All right. So one of the things that you get from entering a new market is the opportunity to build something and put it in customers’ homes and learn a lot about what matters and what doesn’t matter. So we launched Sonos Ace two years ago. I think measured against any of the other premium over-the-ear noise-canceling headphones in the market, they’re a great product. They’ve got great reviews; they have great noise cancelling. They’re super comfortable, and they look great. We’re really proud of the product, but they weren’t thoughtfully integrated into the Sonos ecosystem. I mean, at launch you could swap to one of our soundbars, not even all of our soundbars. I think it was the most visible expression of the missed opportunity of that moment for the company to always remember that the products that we make are part of the Sonos system, not individual offerings. So we ended up with a great pair of headphones, but honestly, I mean, you review them all the time; there are lots of great headphones. When we set out to take all the lessons that we learned from Ace to design Ace Ultra, at the very top of that list is that we have to do the hard thing. These headphones have to be able to show up in your home as a part of the system, and the model through which you invoke your headphones has to be completely seamless and delightful. We built an entirely new hardware platform for Ace Ultra called Headphone Engine 2, and it unlocks this capability at the hardware level. And then in Sonos OS 27, we built virtualization so that any one of the speakers in your home can deliver the audio platform to that speaker but can also act as a proxy for your headphones, which don’t have the horsepower to run the full stack — it would kill battery life, et cetera. Now with Ace Ultra, you’ll be able to link your headphones to your Sonos system, walk up to a speaker that’s playing, press a button on your headphones, and the music will jump from the speaker into your headphones. No Bluetooth, no phone. You’ll be able to walk around your whole house, enjoy the music, come to another speaker, press the button again, and it will jump to that speaker using some BLA location-sensing stuff that we’ve developed. It’s super magical. It’s the one job that we had and didn’t deliver on with Ace. We’re really excited to get it out into the market. Analogous to that on the home theater side is, as you mentioned, that we’re making all of our portable speakers — Sonos Play, Sonos Move — capable of being rear channels for home theater. That sounds really easy. Maybe people will even be like, “Why wasn’t that always possible?” But to your point about the deep technology of it, the way that we achieve high-fidelity, low-latency surround experiences in the living room is by directly bonding our rear channel speakers and subwoofer to the soundbar on a proprietary network, not through your access point. So for a speaker to seamlessly hop between being part of your Sonos system as a music node and part of your Sonos system as a surround channel means that you have to do a real-time reconfiguration of that networking stack, and you have to know when to do it. We’re using accelerometers in the product to actually know that you’ve picked it up and set it down in a new location. We’re using Sonos’ positioning system, which is ultrasonic signaling, to broadcast to the room, “Hey, is there a soundbar here?” Ultrasonic comes back saying, “I’m here.” They negotiate position, left and right, and distance, so that they can optimize the surround sound experience. You pick it up again, you take it back to the kitchen, and it’s a regular speaker again. All happens magically, no use of the app. It’s pretty cool. Answer my question on headphones, though. This is my big worry. You’ve got really cool headphones. They have a feature that no one else can ship, and Apple’s going to say, “Look, our new AirPods have Siri AI in them.” You can just say, “Show me what I’m looking at,” and a picture will be taken automatically and something will happen. We’ll get over the privacy implications of that, but that’s a collapse of the headphone market. Maybe. I mean, headphones come in all kinds of form factors today: over-ear, in-ear, cuffs, wireless, wired. So I do think it’s a market where people choose different form factors for different tasks. We’re really focused on this personal in-the-home listening — what do you do when the baby’s asleep? What do you do when you want to move the party from the kitchen to the den while you relax for the evening? We think that there’s a bunch of really interesting use cases there that other people aren’t paying attention to. I think, broadly, over the course of the next couple of years, we’re going to get all kinds of adventurous wackadoodle consumer electronics that are connected to this new emerging AI universe. Most of them will be a swing and a miss. Of course, we’ve already seen some of those. So it’s a little hard to speculate, I think, about which of these things, if any, is going to have its iPod moment or its iPhone moment or whatever. What do you think is going to happen? I think we’re going to see a replay of what happened when the headphone jack got taken away. The headphone jack was an open interconnect. There was a really vibrant market for all kinds of headphones, and a bunch of those companies don’t exist anymore. The high-end wired headphones, for phones anyway, have mostly gone away, and you have a bunch of medium Bluetooth competitors, but the phone makers have largely taken that with first-party products. Now, you have your products at the high end competing with really high-end noise-canceling products from Bose and Sony and whoever, and that is the airplane set. The lack of the open interconnect has really killed the vibrancy of the low and middle end of the market. Okay, well, there’s one big thing they can do to make sure the high end belongs to them, and it’s to integrate AI in very specific ways directly into their operating system. We’ll see how that plays out. There’s also a thing that’s different this time: there’s a vastly more energized European regulatory environment. Who knows how this will play out? Sure. I can’t tell you, but all that stuff is a swirl, and you’re a headphone maker, and it seems like different headphone makers are taking different approaches to this. The only counter that I might offer is that there’s a lot of talk about the walled garden of the Bluetooth advantages that the platform companies have. But I would say even without the European regulators, it’s notable that something like the Meta Glasses can have a reasonable, I think, commercially viable set of experiences that are principally powered by compute that lives on your phone and still deliver conversational AI that is mediated by a Bluetooth connection, admittedly behind some of the obstacles that you’re describing. But those obstacles aren’t so profound that clever companies aren’t figuring out how to work within those constraints. I’m very curious to see how that plays out. It doesn’t seem like it’s in focus. Again, probably because, as you say, none of the products are in focus. No one knows what a hit product here looks like, so you might as well let a thousand flowers bloom and then radically constrict the market. Yeah, sure. Tom, I’ve burned just a ton of your time. I think you can tell I could talk to you for ages and ages about all kinds of things. Super fun. Tell us what’s next for Sonos. When does all this stuff ship? So I think by the time this airs, we’ll have announced all of this to the world. We’re having a big event in New York to share Sonos OS 27, Sonos Voice 27, and the Ace Ultra and Beam Ultra. We can’t wait to get this stuff out into the world and begin to hear what our customers do with all of these exciting new products. Many of the software features are going to be available in early access, which will mean our customers will opt into them, be able to give us feedback, and we’ll be able to observe the telemetry that comes back from their homes and make sure that we’re delivering exactly the experience that we want. We’re excited about the moment of co-creation that’s around the corner for us. As we talked about at the top of the hour, Sonos 27 is absolutely a nod to the fact that we intend to keep doing this until the sun burns out. There’ll be Sonos 28 and 29 and 30 and beyond. That’s great. All right, I’ve got to ask you at the end: I have ceiling speakers in my kitchen. They’re connected to a Sonos Amp. There’s a Google Home Hub right there, and it’s broken. I can’t ask it to play music in the kitchen. When are you going to fix that for me? I’m ending on tech support. All right. I don’t know the answer, but I’d love to figure it out for you. I know the right folks to call, so let’s get you connected. We’re going to have a Decoder roundtable. If your listeners have similar kinds of problems, we’ve got great people to help them, and we always like to hear from you. You can find me on social pretty easily. Usually I end by inviting people back, but I’m saying we’ve got to fix it, and then we’re going to talk about what it took to fix it. That’s the plan. All right. Right on. Tom, this is great. Thank you so much, man. This was super fun. Thank you. Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!

noticias.titulo: Repeal of U.S. Roadless Rule could threaten drinking water for 25 million people
noticias.resumen: The drinking water for about 25 million Americans starts in the backcountry of the national forests, on land where roads are few by design. A rule the Trump administration proposed last week could open that land to roads and logging. On Aug. 18, the U.S. Department of Agriculture filed a proposed rule to fully rescind […]
noticias.contenido: The drinking water for about 25 million Americans starts in the backcountry of the national forests, on land where roads are few by design. A rule the Trump administration proposed last week could open that land to roads and logging. On Aug. 18, the U.S. Department of Agriculture filed a proposed rule to fully rescind the U.S. Forest Service’s 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule, which bars new road construction and commercial logging on about 45 million acres (18 million hectares) of national forest. It was published in the Federal Register on Aug. 20, opening a 30-day public comment period that closes at midnight on Sept. 21. The proposed rule has drawn widespread criticism among wildland firefighters, environmental organizations, lawmakers and scientists. Much of the debate has centered on logging and fire. But researchers say some of the largest costs run downstream, into the taps of people’s homes. Wilder Mountain Inventoried Roadless Area ,Green Mountain National Forest in Vermont. Photo courtesy of Zack Porter / Standing Trees. Forests work as natural filters. They intercept rain, slow runoff, and trap sediment before water reaches streams, rivers and reservoirs. Roads and logging can undo that work, casting off sediment that utility companies must clean and driving up treatment costs. A 2024 study in Forests found that forest roads contribute up to 90 percent of sediment loads in streams and are “seriously disrupting the safety and stability of watersheds.” A study published in July in PLOS Water estimated that about 25 million Americans draw…This article was originally published on Mongabay

noticias.titulo: Irán ataca objetivos de EE.UU. en Kuwait pese a las amenazas de Trump
noticias.resumen: El Ejército kuwaití afirmó que había interceptado un ataque con misiles y drones; los combates se intensificaron esta semana después de que Washington atacara el domingo lanzacohetes iraníes
noticias.contenido: TEHERÁN.– Irán volvió a atacar objetivos militares norteamericanos en Kuwait el jueves, mientras hace caso omiso a las amenazas del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , y sigue adelante con las represalias por los bombardeos de Washington a principios de semana. El Ejército de Kuwait afirmó que había interceptado un ataque con misiles y drones procedentes de Irán. Teherán detalló que había atacado la base aérea de Ahmad al Jaber , en territorio kuwaití, “con misiles y drones”. Kuwait calificó los ataques como una “amenaza directa para su seguridad y estabilidad” , y una “grave violación de las normas del derecho internacional”. El Ejército de Irán también aseguró que había atacado la base aérea de Al-Minhad, en Emiratos Árabes Unidos , pero este país del Golfo no informó de ningún ataque de este tipo. El día anterior, Irán había prometido hacer “pedazos” al enemigo estadounidense , luego de ataques a su territorio que, entre otros objetivos, alcanzaron una boda . Según Teherán, los bombardeos dejaron un total de 19 muertos , entre ellos siete miembros de las fuerzas armadas y también civiles, uno de los balances más elevados de los últimos meses. Cuatro de las víctimas asistían a unas nupcias en el distrito de Sirik, en el sureste del país, donde cerca de 70 personas resultaron heridas según los medios estatales. Nueva escalada en Medio Oriente Las sirenas se activaron en Kuwait a primera hora del jueves y las defensas antiaéreas interceptaron ataques con misiles y drones durante una “flagrante agresión iraní”, dijo el Ministerio de Defensa del país en X. Esto ocurrió después de que Bahréin y Jordania , aliados de Estados Unidos, afirmaron que sus sistemas de defensa aérea también habían interceptado varios ataques aéreos iraníes el miércoles. Los combates entre Estados Unidos e Irán se han intensificado esta semana después de que Washington atacara el domingo lanzacohetes iraníes en una isla del estrecho de Ormuz , alegando que Teherán planeaba utilizarlos para disparar minas hacia la vía crucial navegable. Desde que empezó el conflicto, el régimen islámico ha bloqueado la crucial vía marítima –por la que antes de la guerra transitaban el 20% de las exportaciones mundiales de petróleo y gas natural licuado–, y ha logrado mantener la actividad comercial al mínimo, salvo en ocasiones puntuales. El presidente norteamericano propuso el miércoles rebautizar el corredor como el de “estrecho de Trump” , aunque más tarde dio a entender que no hablaba en serio ante una pregunta de la AFP al respecto. Según indicó el mismo día la Guardia de la Revolución iraní, dos petroleros se incendiaron tras chocar con minas en el Golfo , al transitar fuera del itinerario designado por las autoridades de Teherán. Como parte de su promesa de someter a la república islámica a una “asfixia” económica, Washington impuso un bloqueo a los puertos iraníes y, recientemente, una nueva ronda de sanciones secundarias contra los socios comerciales de Teherán. En este escenario, los mercados del petróleo volvieron a sentir el golpe y en medio de una inquietud generalizada pasaron a operar al alza el jueves. Poco después de las 7.00 hora de la Argentina, el precio del barril de Brent del Mar del Norte para entrega en noviembre subía un 1,24%, hasta los 96,82 dólares . Su equivalente estadounidense, el barril de West Texas Intermediate para entrega en octubre, subía un 1,36%, hasta los 92,25 dólares . Condena y advertencia de Irán Teherán advirtió el miércoles que aplicará una “nueva estrategia” en la guerra que iniciaron Estados Unidos e Israel en su contra a finales de febrero. “Pronto verán que la nueva estrategia de Irán en el campo de batalla, en la diplomacia y en la confrontación del bloqueo económico , hará pedazos sus cimientos”, publicó en X el secretario del Consejo Supremo de Seguridad Nacional de Irán, Mohsen Rezai , sin dar más detalles. El principal negociador y presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohamad Baqer Qalibaf , calificó a Estados Unidos de “Satán” tras el ataque a la boda , recordando además el bombardeo de una escuela en Minab que, según Teherán, mató a 155 personas , entre ellas 120 chicos , en las primeras horas de la guerra, el 28 de febrero. Sin aludir directamente una ofensiva contra la ceremonia nupcial, el Comando de Estados Unidos para Medio Oriente dijo que sus fuerzas “nunca atacan a civiles, a diferencia de los Guardianes de la Revolución” . Las imágenes que muestran los daños en el lugar donde se llevaba a cabo el casamiento se han difundido ampliamente en Irán. El portavoz de la diplomacia iraní, Esmail Baqai , condenó un “crimen de guerra” , al lamentar que “una ceremonia de boda haya sido brutalmente bombardeada en el marco de la lucha desesperada de Estados Unidos por ocultar su fracaso”. Agencias AP, AFP y ANSA

noticias.contenido: Septiembre es el mes en el que los cuadernos nuevos y las listas interminables de material escolar toman el control de la rutina diaria. Como padre, puedo asegurarte que la Vuelta al Cole no es solo abastecer la mochila de los niños sino también equipar la casa para que el curso transcurra con orden y el menor número de imprevistos posible. A lo largo de los años he aprendido que gastar en gadgets aleatorios suelen terminar en un cajón. Sin embargo, hay una serie de productos indispensables que salvan el día a día aunque no lo creas. Estos son los " must have " en los que realmente merece la pena invertir. Impresora térmica portátil Phomemo D30 por 19,99 euros : se conecta mediante Bluetooth y sus pegatinas son impermeables. Escritorio elevable Flexispot E1 por 169,99 euros : con cuatro funciones de memoria. Mochila Eastpak Provider por 65,99 euros : de 33 litros e ideal para portátiles de hasta 15 pulgadas. Tablet Lenovo Idea Tab por 189 euros : con Android 15 y 128 GB de almacenamiento interno. Localizador Apple AirTag 2ª gen por 26 euros : con búsqueda de precisión y autonomía de un año. Impresora térmica de pegatinas para el material Perder chaquetas, botellas de agua o lápices es un clásico de todos los años. Las antiguas etiquetas escritas a mano terminan borrándose con los lavados o despegándose. Por eso, lo mejor es adquirir una mini impresora térmica portátil con el que ahorrarás horas de preparación durante el fin de semana previo al inicio de las clases. Te permite marcar uniformes, fiambreras y material de papelería en segundos y sin usar tinta. Un modelo barato que te recomiendo es esta Phomemo D30 ( 19,99 euros en Amazon). Es una mini impresora térmica de bolsillo que se conecta al móvil a través de Bluetooth . Los rollos de pegatinas son impermeables y resistentes al lavavajillas. Escritorio elevable Nuestros hijos crecen a un ritmo vertiginoso y pasar de hacer los deberes en la mesa del salón a tener su propio rincón de estudio exige cuidar la ergonomía desde pequeños. Es por eso que yo te recomendaría un escritorio elevable motorizado, ya que se puede adaptar al crecimiento a lo largo de los años y te evita renovar el mobiliario cada cierto tiempo. Un modelo de escritorio elevable que me gustaría recomendarte es el Flexispot E1 , que puedes comprar por 169,99 euros . Aunque a priori te parezca caro, es una buena inversión a largo plazo. Está disponible en diferentes medidas y cuenta con cuatro funciones de memoria y un motor que trabaja con un nivel bajo de ruido. Mochila ergonómica con compartimento acolchado para el portátil o tablet El peso de los libros y la integración paulatina de dispositivos digitales en las clases hacen que cualquier mochila no sirva. A la hora de comprar una mochila, priorizaría un modelo con correas acolchadas, distribución equilibrada del peso y funda de protección para la tablet o el portátil, ya que todo esto es clave para evitar dolores de espalda. Una buena mochila que puedes comprar para la Vuelta al Cole es esta Eastpak Provider (rebajada a 65,99 euros ). Tiene una capacidad de 33 litros y tiene una funda acolchada para portátiles de hasta 15 pulgadas, además de un asa de goma para llevarla más cómodamente. En Xataka Vuelta al Cole en Carrefour: los cinco mejores chollos para equipar tu zona de trabajo o estudio en casa con la mejor tecnología Tablet con modo lectura/estudio y control parental integrado La tecnología es una herramienta indispensable para el aprendizaje actual, pero la línea entre el estudio y la distracción digital es muy fina. En lugar de reciclar un móvil antiguo o comprar una tablet genérica, apostar por un dispositivo con pantalla de protección ocular (modo lectura / tinta electrónica) y un control parental nativo bien configurado permite a los niños buscar información o leer libros escolares sin caer en las interrupciones de las redes sociales o los juegos. Una tablet totalmente recomendable para esta vuelta a las clases es la Lenovo Idea Tab , un modelo de 11 pulgadas que puedes comprar ahora por 189 euros en MediaMarkt en su versión de 4 GB de RAM y 128 GB de almacenamiento. El sistema operativo bajo el que funciona es Android 15 e incluye el lápiz digital Tab Pen. Localizador para la mochila o el estuche Para la tranquilidad mental de los padres cuando nuestros hijos empiezan a ir solos al colegio o realizan actividades extraexcolares, poner un l ocalizador Bluetooth en un bolsillo interno de la mochila nos permite saber si ha llegado bien al colegio y, además, soluciona el drama de que la olvide en el parque o el entrenamiento deportivo. Si tienes un iPhone, el localizador más completo que puedes comprar es el AirTag (ahora está disponible por 26 euros en Amazon el de segunda generación). El AirTag de Apple tiene el tamaño de una moneda grande y una batería que dura en torno a un año. Además, ofrece búsqueda de precisión al utilizar tecnología de banda ultraancha (UWB). En Xataka Vuelta al Cole en MediaMarkt: las mejores ofertas que hemos encontrado hoy, 31 de agosto También pueden interesarte Nota: algunos de los enlaces aquí publicados son de afiliados y pueden reportar un beneficio. noticias.titulo: Qué dijo Donald Trump sobre las islas Malvinas que provocó reacciones en la Argentina y Reino Unido
noticias.resumen: El presidente estadounidense volvió a referirse al conflicto bélico y al histórico reclamo nacional; “Aún queda mucho camino por recorrer”, afirmó, sin dar mayores precisiones
noticias.contenido: La sugerencia de Donald Trump de que su administración podría retirarle el apoyo a Reino Unido en medio de la disputa con la Argentina por la soberanía de las islas Malvinas activó una escalada de declaraciones internacionales. Este jueves, el presidente estadounidense redobló la apuesta y evitó responder si continuaría apoyando a Londres ante el reclamo argentino. Al ser consultado por sus declaraciones sobre las Malvinas, el mandatario republicano explicó: “Bueno, yo estuve allí cuando tuvieron la primera guerra. Eso fue hace mucho tiempo y lo observé con mucha atención, y ustedes se comportaron muy bien ”. En una entrevista con GB News , añadió: “Las recuperaron con bastante fuerza, pero aún queda mucho camino por recorrer. Es un viaje largo, está muy lejos .” Las palabras llegaron horas antes de la cadena nacional que anunció el presidente Javier Milei para este jueves por la noche, en la que brindará más detalles sobre el avance en las negociaciones por las islas Malvinas . En otro tramo de la conversación con el medio inglés, Trump también se refirió a la falta de apoyo que recibió por parte de Reino Unido durante la guerra en Irán . “ Tu país no está yendo bien . No se olviden de que obtiene un gran porcentaje de su petróleo del estrecho de Ormuz , y no estuvieron allí para ayudarme ”, apuntó el primer mandatario. En declaraciones que habían generado sorpresa el lunes, el presidente estadounidense ya había sugerido la posible ruptura con su histórico aliado. “ Siempre reviso todas las posiciones. Esa es apenas una entre muchas ”, fue la respuesta de Trump en el Salón Oval ante la consulta específica sobre Malvinas de un periodista. Esa fue la primera vez que el mandatario republicano se pronunció en ese sentido. La declaración de Trump se registró luego de que la semana pasada el diario británico The Telegraph revelara que Estados Unidos, a través de funcionarios del Pentágono, había amenazado a Reino Unido con cambiar su posicionamiento sobre las Malvinas en caso de que el gobierno del primer ministro Andy Burnham no aumentara el gasto en Defensa. De acuerdo al artículo publicado por The Telegraph , la advertencia estadounidense de modificar su postura sobre las Malvinas figura entre una serie de medidas que analizan altos funcionarios del Pentágono para así incentivar a que los miembros de la OTAN lleven al 5% de su PBI la inversión en materia de defensa, como pretende Trump. Respuesta de Reino Unido Luego de la advertencia de Trump, un vocero del gobierno británico ratificó la soberanía sobre las islas y aseguró que su postura es “ clarísima ”. “Los habitantes de las Falklands (nombre que le dan los ingleses a Malvinas) son británicos y tienen derecho a determinar su propio futuro. Expresaron su deseo de seguir siendo un territorio británico de ultramar y nuestro compromiso con ellos es inquebrantable”, afirmó el funcionario del primer ministro Andy Burnham en declaraciones consignadas por el medio inglés The Guardian . Este martes el portavoz aseguró que el primer ministro dejó en claro desde su primer día en el cargo —que asumió el pasado 20 de julio— que cumplirá con sus “compromisos internacionales con sus aliados en materia de gasto en defensa ” y que “no cambió de opinión al respecto”. Según el medio británico, el conflicto con Trump se produjo tras supuestas versiones que apuntaban a que John Healey, ministro de Hacienda británico, iba a abandonar el compromiso previo de Reino Unido de destinar el 3% de su PIB al gasto en defensa para 2030 , cuando presente su primer presupuesto el 28 de octubre.

noticias.titulo: Nvidia buys Hugging Face, the GitHub of AI, for $13 billion
noticias.resumen: Nvidia said Hugging Face hosts over 3 million models and is used by over 18 million developers.
noticias.contenido: Nvidia has agreed to buy AI model platform Hugging Face for $13 billion, in the latest step by the $5.4 trillion chip giant to use its financial might to accelerate the technology’s boom while exerting greater control over the industry. Hugging Face, which only last year turned down a large investment from Nvidia at a $7 billion valuation to maintain its independence, serves as a repository for millions of models and data sets and has become a champion of “open” AI systems. Nvidia said the goal of the deal was to speed up the spread of open models. Unlike proprietary models from labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, the design of open-weight models is public and users can download, customize and run them on their own hardware. noticias.contenido: En 1976, un equipo canadiense dirigido por David Schindler vertió ácido sulfúrico sobre un pequeño lago al noroeste de Ontario. Era un lago normal. Con sus sedimentos, sus corrientes, sus truchas y sus crustáceos. No quería un experimento de laboratorio, ni un modelo de ordenador: quería simular el efecto de la lluvia ácida en el entorno. Por eso, volvieron a la semana siguiente y a siguiente. Durante 17 años estuvieron vertiendo ácido en el lago 223 de la Experimental Lakes Area . Aquello calló la boca a la industria del carbón que llevaba años negando la relación entre sus emisiones y los muchos lagos muertos de Escandinavia y Norteamérica, sí; pero costó un lago. Un lago como probeta. Desde el comienzo del experimento, los investigadores constataron que el pH del agua fue bajando desde el 6,8 del 76 al 5,0-5,1 de 1981. El equipo mantuvo ese pH hasta 1988 y luego empezó a gestionar su ascenso poco a poco. Ni que decir tiene que el lago estaba reventado, pero aprendimos cosas en el proceso. Para empezar, no todas las especies se mueren de golpe. El Pimephales promelas colapsó rápido una vez se llegó al 5,6 ; la trucha de lago ( Salvelinus namaycush ) dejó de reproducirse a 5,4; y el matalote blanco aguantó hasta 5,1. De hecho, la trucha ni siquiera se murió envenenada. Por eso he dicho "dejó de reproducirse". Lo que pasó es que se quedó sin relevo generacional : murieron viejas y solas . En Xataka EEUU tiene un problema tan grande con la carpa asiática en sus ríos que ha decidido algo extremo: electrocutarlas La lenta vuelta a normalidad . Con la evidencia de lo que había pasado en ese lago, las autoridades empezaron a legislar. Aunque poco reconocidos, sus datos fueron clave para el Acuerdo de Calidad del Aire entre Canadá y Estados Unidos de 1991 y, un poco más tarde, para el Convenio de Ginebra. Durante los siguientes trece años, los investigadores hicieron un minucuioso seguimiento del proceso de recuperación del lago. El pH del agua se recuperó desde el 5,1 al 6,7 y eso hizo que especies como el Pimephales promelas volvieran al lago o la población del matalote blanco se disparara hasta por diez. Lo que no volvió fue la trucha. Treinta años después de dejar de verter ácido al agua, la población de este pez sigue por la mitad de la que había a mediados de los 70. De hecho, las que hay que crecen más lento y acumulan más mercurio que las que viven en otros lagos de la zona. Pero... ¿por qué? Durante estos años los expertos le han dado muchas vueltas al asunto. ¿Qué estaba pasando? ¿Acaso no habían conseguido solucionar el problema reproductivo de las truchas? Y sí. Lo que pasa es que, una vez subsanado ese asunto, el problema era otro: la cadena trófica estaba rota por un eslabón pequeñísimo, pero fundamental: las gambas. El Mysis diluviana es un pequeño crustáceo (con forma de camarón diminuto) que vive en los lagos profundos y fríos de América del Norte. Estas gambas eran básicas en la dieta de las truchas y, según los análisis del ADN sedimentado en el fondo, desaparecieron muy pronto del lago: en 1979 ya no quedaba ninguno. Es algo curioso porque, en fin, los investigadores siempre habían pensando que en el 79 todo estaba bien. ¿Y si lo solucionamos a mano? Eso se dijeron y pusieron en marcha el proyecto SHRRIMP ( Stenotherm Habitat Restoration through Recolonization of Mysis Project ). Se trata de una iniciativa muy básica: echar 10.000 crustáceos al lago dos veces al año (en primavera y otoño). Empezaron a 2018 y para 2021 la población de gambas estaba recuperada. Y, ojo, es la primera vez que ocurre . Ahora mismo los investigadores están estudiando si es suficiente. Hay muchas otras cosas que podrían salir mal (los sedimentos, el calcio lixiviado en el suelo, los cambio del clima en estos años, etc...), pero reconforta saber que, como dice nuestra carcinóloga de referencia , pase lo que pase, las gambas siempre son una solución a todos los problemas. Acabó tan mal que solo había una cosa que podía salvarlo: cubos y cubos de gambas fue publicada originalmente en Xataka por Javier Jiménez .

noticias.titulo: NASA’s Hubble Spies Superbubble Scene
noticias.resumen: This Hubble Space Telescope image features a sprawling cosmic vista called N44.
noticias.contenido: Explore Hubble Hubble Home Overview About Hubble The History of Hubble Hubble Timeline Why Have a Telescope in Space? Hubble by the Numbers At the Museum FAQs Impact & Benefits Hubble’s Impact & Benefits Science Impacts Cultural Impact Technology Benefits Impact on Human Spaceflight Astro Community Impacts Science Hubble Science Science Themes Science Highlights Science Behind Discoveries Universe Uncovered Hubble’s Partners in Science Hubble & Citizen Science AI & Hubble Science Explore the Night Sky Observatory Hubble Observatory Hubble Design Mission Operations Science Operations Astronaut Missions to Hubble Hubble vs. Webb Hubble vs. Roman Team Hubble Team Career Aspirations Hubble Astronauts Multimedia Images Videos Online Activities e-Books Sonifications Podcasts 3D Hubble Models Lithographs Fact Sheets Posters Hubble on the NASA App Glossary News Hubble News Social Media Media Resources 35th Anniversary More Online Activities 3 min read NASA’s Hubble Spies Superbubble Scene This Hubble Space Telescope image features the picturesque nebula LHA 120-N44, or N44. NASA, ESA/Hubble, D. Gouliermis This NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image features a sprawling cosmic vista in the Large Magellanic Cloud, or LMC, the largest of the small galaxies that orbit our Milky Way galaxy. At just 160,000 light-years away, the LMC offers a close look at highly active star birth sites like the one in this image. This photogenic nebula, named LHA 120-N44, or N44, is in the constellation Dorado. N44 is dominated by two features: a vast central void and a shell of dense, dusty gas. The central void is a ‘superbubble’ spanning roughly 210 by 140 light-years across. The glittering stars at the center of the void are responsible for its creation; through their powerful stellar winds and explosive supernovae, these stars expelled much of the gas from which they were born. When the stars of N44’s central star cluster swept away this gas, the expelled gas compressed and formed a shell around the superbubble. New stars are forming in this compressed gas shell, making N44 an interesting target for astronomers who are using the nebula to study how stars form in this environment. Their goal is to understand how long it takes from the collapse of cold gas clouds into dense knots to the moment nuclear fusion ignites in the heart of a newborn star. The data in this image is from an observing program ( #14689 ; PI: Gouliermis) that used Hubble to survey N44 and take a census of its stars, cataloging nearly half a million stars within the cluster as well as interlopers drifting in front of it. Of the stars surveyed, nearly 30,000 are what astronomers call pre-main-sequence stars, which have yet to begin fusing hydrogen into helium in their cores. Astronomers discovered this treasure trove of baby stars thanks to the high sensitivity and fine spatial resolution of Hubble’s instruments that can pick out faint objects in crowded clusters. The gas shell surrounding the superbubble is energized by ultraviolet radiation from massive stars, causing it to glow and highlighting several distinct features. Each feature within the broader N44 star-forming complex was cataloged by astronomer Karl Henize in the 1950s. One feature is a smaller bubble, cataloged as N44F, that is located near the upper-right corner of this image. N44F is an interstellar bubble blown by the intense stellar winds of a single hot and massive star. As this previously released Hubble closeup shows, the star’s furious winds and radiation have sculpted the surrounding bubble and created pillars of dusty gas. Hubble’s sensitive observations of the lowest-mass stars in this region open a new window onto star formation in regions that, like the LMC or the galaxies in the early universe, are poor in elements heavier than helium. Text Credit: ESA/Hubble Facebook logo @NASAHubble @NASAHubble Instagram logo @NASAHubble Media Contact : Claire Andreoli NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center , Greenbelt, MD claire.andreoli@nasa.gov Explore More Hubble’s Inside The Image: N44 Superbubble In this YouTube video, Dr. Ken Carpenter takes us on a journey through the Nebula, teaching us some of the interesting science behind this famous Hubble image. Hubble Views N44 Superbubble N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble image in the upper central region. From seizure to sentence: Weak prosecution leaves tigers vulnerable to trafficking in Southeast Asia: Report
noticias.resumen: When tiger poachers and traffickers are apprehended in Southeast Asia, they frequently get away without consequences: Fewer than half of arrests and seizures in the cat’s Southeast Asian range countries are backed up by penalties or convictions, according to a recently published report by Canadian conservation think tank the GuArdean Centre for Conservation Research, wildlife […]
noticias.contenido: When tiger poachers and traffickers are apprehended in Southeast Asia, they frequently get away without consequences: Fewer than half of arrests and seizures in the cat’s Southeast Asian range countries are backed up by penalties or convictions, according to a recently published report by Canadian conservation think tank the GuArdean Centre for Conservation Research, wildlife trade watchdog TRAFFIC, and WWF International. This means there’s little deterrent for a lucrative illegal industry that’s driving tigers toward extinction, experts say. Black market trade in their skins, bones, teeth and other body parts is an extremely lucrative business; most are headed to China, the top consumer. Researchers assessed publicly available records related to 259 tiger-related seizures in Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos between 2019 and 2024 — seven of the 10 countries where wild tigers still survive. Heather Sohl, the tiger trade lead at WWF and a co-author of the report, noted that these cases represent just a fraction of the trade, “only those which were intercepted and reported.” That level of wildlife crime could have a “massive impact” on wild tiger populations, she said. Based on their findings, the study’s authors are calling for a raft of measures to strengthen sentencing in an effort to fight the international criminal organizations that mastermind tiger trade and other wildlife crime in the region. noticias.contenido: “Development bank-backed transition minerals projects are frequently associated with significant environmental, social, and human rights risks.” This is the conclusion of the latest report by the International Accountability Project (IAP), an international advocacy organization. IAP analyzed 77 projects globally, approved between 2023 and 2025. The analysis resulted in the Transition Minerals Finance Tracker, an interactive online database documenting transition minerals projects. It reveals that more than half of the projects analyzed, and nearly three-quarters of African projects, show evidence of actual, probable or potential harm to local communities. “There are many companies that are multinational mining corporations who have a very bad track record in terms of human rights, yet they do get loans from the development banks,” Vaishnavi Varadarajan, program coordinator at IAP, told Mongabay in a phone interview. “It is raising the question of the due diligence that is being done by the banks beforehand.” Since the Paris Agreement in 2015, a growing number of countries are investing in renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power as well as electric vehicles to limit their greenhouse gas emissions. Such technologies require components made from minerals and rare earth elements that are often found in the Global South and shipped to the Global North for value-added processing, Varadarajan said. “[I]t is kind of reinforcing a colonial way of extraction.” The report denounces an unfair transition, in which countries financing extraction reap most of the economic benefits, while countries where raw materials are located face water depletion and contamination,…This article was originally published on Mongabay

noticias.contenido: Poco antes de las 8:00 de la mañana del 1 de septiembre, la zona central del Palacio de los Hurtado de Mendoza, en Almazán (Soria), cedió. Dos plantas cayeron de golpe, arrastrando el artesonado, los arcos y los fustes de la galería superior sobre la galería gótica de abajo: 5 de sus 11 arcos originales ya no están en pie. Piedra y madera bajaron rodando por la ladera hasta la ronda del Duero. La torre y parte de las arquerías siguen en pie, pero el boquete en la fachada deja el interior del edificio como si un cañonazo la hubiera alcanzado. El edificio, en cifras. Lo levantó a finales del siglo XV Pedro González de Mendoza y Luna, primer conde de Monteagudo y guarda mayor de Enrique IV; también se le conoce como Palacio de los Condes de Altamira. Entre abril y junio de 1496 alojó a los Reyes Católicos. Fue declarado Bien de Interés Cultural, categoría Monumento, en 1991. Ese sello protege el edificio sobre el papel, no lo sostiene en pie: la Junta movilizó técnicos de Patrimonio el mismo día del derrumbe, no antes. "Era previsible". Así lo calificó el alcalde de Almazán , Jesús Cedazo, que lleva años pidiendo la rehabilitación del palacio a Patrimonio sin respuesta. Un edificio protegido desde 1991 tardó 35 años en desplomarse mientras esperaba una obra que nunca llegó. Justo a la altura del puente, el siniestro obligó a cortar al tráfico la CL-116A, un tramo de aproximadamente 500 metros que conecta la N-111. Al menos hasta descartar el riesgo de nuevos desprendimientos. La gran pregunta es: ¿cuántos castillos están ahora mismo en las mismas condiciones, a punto de rendirse? Tower defense. En marzo, un turista grabó con el móvil cómo la torre albarrana del castillo de Escalona (Toledo) se venía abajo en 5 segundos. Un año antes, en abril de 2025, cayó una torre del castillo de Almonacid, también en Toledo, tras semanas de lluvia. Los tres edificios comparten protección BIC y estado ruinoso. Solo el 20% de los castillos españoles se considera rehabilitado y en estado aceptable; el 80% restante arrastra problemas de conservación más o menos graves, según la misma asociación. Una catedral conserva su función y sigue recibiendo culto; un castillo, usualmente no. Acaso cuenta con un par de salas museizadas, tienda de souvenirs y poco más. En Xataka Mark Zuckerberg ya estaba considerado como un señor tecnofeudal. Ahora también tiene su castillo Los números que faltan. España no sabe cuántos castillos tiene. El catálogo oficial del Ministerio de Cultura es de 1968 y resulta insuficiente; el recuento más completo lo lleva una asociación privada, la Asociación Española de Amigos de los Castillos, con 10.362 fortificaciones censadas . De esas, solo 728 están en muy buen estado, 2.209 en buen estado, 1.037 en estado regular, 537 en "ruinas consolidadas" y 2.087 en "ruina progresiva". Ante desprendimientos como el de 15 metros en Salamanca , Lugo o los muchos desprendimientos en Plasencia , el arqueólogo Miguel Ángel Bru dio la cifra clave: 6 de cada 10 castillos corren riesgo de venirse abajo. Parte del problema es la propiedad: hay castillos repartidos entre decenas de herederos que ni siquiera saben que poseen un trozo de fortaleza. Cómo lo hacen otros. Francia financia su patrimonio con una lotería propia: el Loto du Patrimoine , lanzado en 2018, recauda entre 15 y 20 millones de euros al año y ya financió la restauración de más de 980 sitios, castillos incluidos; en 2026 seleccionó 100 monumentos nuevos, uno por departamento. Reino Unido publica desde 1998 un registro público de edificios en riesgo, el Heritage at Risk Register : 4.891 entradas en 2024, 7,4 millones de libras en ayudas solo el último año y 6.800 inmuebles rescatados entre 1998 y 2023. España tiene desde 1985 su propio mecanismo, el 1% Cultural, que obliga a destinar parte del presupuesto de obra pública al patrimonio. Ni Almazán ni Escalona ni Almonacid llegaron a beneficiarse de él a tiempo. Reutilizando, que es gerundio . Parece que España tiene una relación reacia con sus edificios históricos: conservarlos suele significar mantenerlos lo más cerca posible de su función original, aunque esa función haya desaparecido hace siglos. Repensar usos concedería una segunda vida. En Países Bajos, donde alrededor de 75 iglesias cierran cada año, antiguos templos acabaron convertidos en discotecas , viviendas , bibliotecas, gimnasios, restaurantes y hasta pistas de pádel . No hay remilgo al expropio porque, de facto, se ayuda a propietarios a dar con nuevas formas de financiación. En Francia , antiguos castillos pasaron a ser ayuntamientos, bibliotecas o museos, mientras fortalezas militares se integraron en circuitos culturales. Irlanda sigue la misma lógica: si un edificio histórico ya no sirve para lo que nació, se busca otra función que permita mantenerlo vivo (el castillo de Rathfarnham es un buen ejemplo). Patrimonio congelado no es patrimonio intacto, es una herida abierta. En una tierra con miles de castillos, conventos, iglesias y edificios defensivos que ya no cumplen ninguna función, tal vez la clave reside justo ahí. Memoria en ruinas. Almazán llevaba 35 años de plazo, cinco siglos de historia y ninguna partida presupuestaria que tomara medidas. Sin embargo, los castillos o palacios medievales, erigidos con las manos del pueblo, ya no evocan el pasado feudalista, sino que son, imperativamente, el nodo físico de la propia memoria colectiva de cada pueblo. El BOE registra partidas fundamentales como la Ley de Memoria Democrática, pero es una cifra nimia si comparamos: un solo ejercicio del Loto du Patrimoine francés la multiplica por más de 10. Parece que la gravedad no es tanto olvidar como ignorar. Esta semana ha caído fue publicada originalmente en Xataka por Isra Fdez .

noticias.resumen: James Cartlidge apuntó contra la cadena nacional que dará el primer mandatario argentino este jueves por la noche; destacó el “sacrificio” de los soldados que murieron en la Guerra de Malvinas
noticias.contenido: El parlamentario inglés James Cartlidge se sumó a la polémica por la soberanía de las islas Malvinas que involucró en los últimos días al presidente Javier Milei y a su par estadounidense Donald Trump , luego de que este último asegurara que su administración podría retirar el apoyo histórico a Reino Unido . El legislador reaccionó a la noticia de la cadena nacional que realizará el presidente argentino este jueves y aseguró que las Malvinas “son británicas” . El referente de Defensa del Partido Conservador en Reino Unido contestó este miércoles en su cuenta de la red social X a un posteo de otro usuario que se hacía eco del anuncio del mensaje de este jueves de Milei, en el que el primer mandatario anticipó que hablará sobre avances en la negociación por la causa Malvinas . “ Las Falklands (nombre que le asigna el Reino Unido a Malvinas) son británicas y seguirán siendo británicas ”, subrayó en este marco Cartlidge y añadió: “Los soldados británicos lucharon y murieron para defender nuestra soberanía y la libertad de los habitantes de las Malvinas. Ese sacrificio nunca será olvidado. Siempre estaremos al lado del pueblo de las Falklands y su abrumador deseo de permanecer como británicos ”. “Pasó algo fuerte respecto de la causa más sagrada que tenemos los argentinos”, había dicho Milei en diálogo con El Observador y en alusión a la afirmación de Trump. Asimismo, y tras la reunión de gabinete de este martes, se decidió que el jueves por la noche el Presidente realice una cadena nacional en donde “brindará mayores detalles a la población sobre este tema”. No trascendieron, hasta el momento, cuáles serían esos detalles . Cartlidge se sumó así a los comentarios que ya había realizado un vocero del gobierno británico , quien ratificó la soberanía sobre el territorio argentino y aseguró que su postura era “ clarísima ”. “Los habitantes de las Malvinas son británicos y tienen derecho a determinar su propio futuro. Expresaron su deseo de seguir siendo un territorio británico de ultramar y nuestro compromiso con ellos es inquebrantable”, afirmó el funcionario del primer ministro Andy Burnham en declaraciones consignadas por el medio inglés The Guardian . Las palabras de Trump tuvieron lugar luego de que la semana pasada el diario británico The Telegraph revelara que Estados Unidos, a través de funcionarios del Pentágono, había amenazado a Reino Unido con cambiar su posicionamiento sobre las Malvinas en caso de que el gobierno no aumentara el gasto en Defensa . En esta misma línea, este martes el portavoz aseguró que el primer ministro dejó en claro desde su primer día en el cargo —que asumió el pasado 20 de julio— que cumplirá con sus “compromisos internacionales con sus aliados en materia de gasto en defensa ” y que “no cambió de opinión al respecto”. Según el medio británico, el conflicto con Trump se produjo tras supuestas versiones que apuntaban a que John Healey, ministro de Hacienda británico, iba a abandonar el compromiso previo de Reino Unido de destinar el 3% de su PIB al gasto en defensa para 2030 , cuando presente su primer presupuesto el 28 de octubre.

noticias.contenido: La reconocida marca de drones y cámaras DJI ha dado un paso firme en el sector de la robótica doméstica con el lanzamiento internacional de su nueva gama de robots aspiradores: la serie ROMO 2 , compuesta por los modelos ROMO P2 y ROMO A2. Aprovechando su experiencia en percepción espacial, la firma china traslada tecnologías desarrolladas para sus aeronaves insignia al suelo del hogar, incorporando Inteligencia Artificial de última generación , detección milimétrica de obstáculos y un innovador sistema mecánico de limpieza. Detección espacial y evitación de obstáculos con IA El núcleo del ROMO 2 es su avanzado sistema de percepción impulsado por IA, diseñado para interpretar el entorno y tomar decisiones de forma autónoma . El robot distingue entre suciedad seca y líquidos, ajustando su comportamiento en tiempo real (aumenta la succión en alfombras o activa la limpieza focalizada en derrames para no esparcirlos). Gracias a su tecnología de navegación, detecta objetos de tan solo 2 mm de grosor (como cables o alfombrillas de mascotas) y es capaz de reconocer e ignorar obstáculos transparentes como cristales o espejos. Está equipado también con un proyector inferior calibrado y con luz de detección nocturna , que le permite identificar suciedad en condiciones de baja luminosidad sin deslumbrar a mascotas o cualquier habitante del hogar. En Xataka Mejores robots aspirador en calidad precio. Cuál comprar en función del uso y seis modelos recomendados Brazo robótico de 123° y 36.000 Pa de potencia En el apartado mecánico, la serie ROMO 2 introduce una estructura adaptativa guiada por un sensor LiDAR integrado . Su brazo robótico de gran alcance ofrece un mecanismo de fregado con oscilación de 123°, lo que le permite ganar 7,8 cm de alcance lateral y profundizar hasta 4,5 cm bajo muebles flotantes. La potencia de succión que ofrece este nuevo DJI ROMO 2 es de 36.000 Pa, convirtiéndose así en un dispositivo ideal para la limpieza de alfombras , ya que una placa de presión crea un semisellado con la superficie para extraer el polvo incrustado en una sola pasada. Por otra parte, las patas robóticas del dispositivo le permiten superar desniveles y escalones de hasta 4 cm en un solo nivel (y hasta 8,5 cm en doble nivel). Además, incorpora 32 materiales aislantes y cámaras silenciadoras que reducen la energía acústica hasta en un 85% operando a unos discretos 85 dB en modo silencioso. En Xataka Llega a Lidl mañana, 4 de septiembre, este foco solar LED con sensor de movimiento por 16,99 euros perfecto para patios y terrazas Estación autolimpiante y enfoque en la privacidad La base de recarga e higienización cuenta con una tabla de lavado nanocristalina que evita la acumulación de suciedad mediante cuatro chorros de agua a alta presión y un puerto de succión de 16 mm, prometiendo hasta 365 días de funcionamiento sin mantenimiento manual . Además, soporta carga rápida de 55 W, alcanzando el 100% de la batería en 2,5 horas. En materia de privacidad, DJI ofrece el modo de datos locales , que permite cortar la conexión de la app a Internet para evitar la sincronización de fotos o mapas con servidores externos, con la opción adicional de desactivar la cámara y el micrófono en cualquier momento. Disponibilidad y precios La serie DJI ROMO 2 se encuentra disponible a partir de este mes de septiembre a través de la tienda oficial de DJI y distribuidores autorizados en las siguientes opciones: DJI ROMO A2 (versión con tanque de agua): desde 1.199 euros. DJI ROMO P2 (versión con tanque de agua): desde 1.299 euros. Pack DJI ROMO Limpia Más: desde 1.349 euros. En caso de no disponibilidad, las ofertas pueden variar.
